t: Mao rose from a peasant family in Hunan to become a founding member of the Chinese Communist Party, built its Red Army on the peasantry and guerrilla warfare, and took the party's leadership during the Long March of 1934-1935.

After defeating the Nationalist government he proclaimed the People's Republic of China in 1949 and led land reform, industrialisation and a series of campaigns against those the party named its enemies.

Under his rule tens of millions died, most in the famine that followed the Great Leap Forward of 1958-1962, and millions were persecuted in the Cultural Revolution; he is also credited with gains in literacy, women's status, health and China's standing as a power.
dyk: In his first article in the radical magazine New Youth, published in April 1917, Mao urged readers to increase their physical strength to serve the revolution; his earliest poem to survive, "Changsha", was written on the eve of the Autumn Harvest Uprising of 1927.
ev: Mao Zedong is born near Shaoshan in Hunan, under the Qing dynasty
He is one of 13 delegates at the first congress of the Chinese Communist Party in Shanghai
The Red Army breaks out of the Jiangxi Soviet and begins the Long March
At the Zunyi conference Mao becomes de facto leader of the party and the Red Army
He proclaims the People's Republic of China from Tiananmen
He launches the Great Leap Forward, followed by the Great Chinese Famine
Mao dies, aged 82, and is succeeded at first by Hua Guofeng

f.born: 26 December 1893, near Shaoshan village in Hunan, under the Qing dynasty; son of Mao Yichang, a formerly impoverished peasant who had become one of Shaoshan's wealthiest farmers, and Wen Qimei
f.died: 9 September 1976, shortly after midnight, aged 82, after years of lung and heart ailments and three heart attacks that year
f.role: Founding member of the Chinese Communist Party (1921); Chairman of the Military Commission (from 1935); Chairman of the Communist Party (from 1943); paramount leader of the People's Republic of China (1949-1976) and its President until 1959
f.known: The Long March; founding the People's Republic of China; land reform and the campaigns against 'counter-revolutionaries'; the Great Leap Forward and the famine that followed; the Cultural Revolution; Mao Zedong Thought and the theory of people's war; the Little Red Book; poetry and calligraphy
